--- page 1 ---
Title/cover page: no figure. Main point: Bangladesh Monsoon Floods AA Framework, 2023 Version, approved by RC 3 Aug 2023, endorsed by USG/ERC OCHA 14 Aug 2023 (contacts updated May 2024); intro + risk/hazard narrative — monsoon floods occur April–September (peak June–Sept), ~1/4 of country inundated in an average year, severe flood every 4–5 years; expands framework to Jamuna + new Padma River basin.

--- page 2 ---
Table (Triggers) comparing Jamuna River vs Padma River: Readiness trigger — Jamuna: water discharge at Bahadurabad gauging station, 3 consecutive days, GloFAS model, max 15-day lead time, >50% likely to cross 1-in-5-year return period. Padma: water discharge at Baruria transit near Goalando station, 3 consecutive days, GloFAS, 12–15 day lead time, >50% likely to cross 1-in-5-year return period. Action trigger — Jamuna: FFWC 5-day lead time model, water level at Bahadurabad crosses "Danger Level" + 0.85 meters, sustained/increasing trend ≥3 consecutive days (GloFAS/RIMES). Padma: FFWC 5-day model, water level at Mawa station crosses 1-in-5-yr return period ("Danger Level" + 0.5 meters), sustained/increasing trend ≥3 days at Baruria transit. Also start of Activation protocol table (Who/What/How/When): BDRCS-led forecast monitoring team (Hassan) monitors GLOFAS/FFWC twice daily via log sheet from June; second row starts on confirming readiness/action triggers.

--- page 3 ---
Continuation of Activation protocol table: BDRCS communicates trigger status to RC/RCO, UN agencies, OCHA, partners via email/WhatsApp incl. intervention map; CERF sends approval letters immediately on readiness/action trigger (pre-approved CERF letter, endorsed by RC/ERC); RC/RCO may convene meeting with BDRCS technical working group, Red Cross/Red Crescent, WFP, FAO, UNFPA, UNICEF, OCHA, government (MoDMR) to discuss coordination (not whether to activate). Narrative: intervention map built on flood depth + population data; priority area list in annex. "Improvements since 2020" list: Padma basin added; GloFAS updated v2.2→3.1 improved readiness trigger skill/lead time (10-day→15-day), doubled successful pre-activations for Jamuna trigger; FFWC water-level forecast has negative bias (underprediction) at longer lead times/high water.

--- page 4 ---
Narrative text, no figure: describes gendered/humanitarian impacts of flooding and lists agency Activities — WFP/BDRCS unconditional cash 4,500 Taka/household via bKash or post office; FAO animal feed at evacuation points + flood-proof storage of agricultural assets; UNICEF safe water (jerricans, purification tablets, mobile water treatment units); UNFPA dignity/menstrual hygiene kits, cash & voucher assistance, WPV deployment, baby kits, mobile SRH camps; BDRCS Flood EAP: unconditional cash to 4,200 families, boat evacuation for 200 families, early warning to ~50,000 people; Save the Children: cash/WASH/evacuation for ~5,000 families (incl. 700 direct cash) in Gaibandha district; Start Fund Bangladesh separate threshold (1-in-5-yr, 10-day forecast, >70% confidence, 3 days) with $750,000 pre-arranged for floods and $600,000 for cyclones.

--- page 5 ---
Map: "Bangladesh Coordinated Anticipatory Action for Monsoon River Flooding" — outline map of Bangladesh showing Jamuna river basin (dark red/red highlight) running north-south through central-north Bangladesh with Bahadurabad station marked, and Padma river basin (light pink highlight) in south-central area with Goalando/Baruria transit and Mawa station marked, relative to Dhaka. Legend: Target districts — Jamuna basin (red) vs Padma basin (pink). Text: 2023 edition expands to 3 more Padma districts (Madaripur, Manikganj, Shariatpur) added to 5 Jamuna districts (Bogra, Jamalpur, Gaibandha, Kurigram [+Sirajganj per annex]); total ~38 Upazilas covered; reach increases by ~20,000 households (100,000 people) to combined 150,000 households; ~1 million people reached via early warning messages.

--- page 6 ---
Table: "Funding overview in US$ for coordinated framework" by agency (WFP, FAO, UNICEF, UNFPA, BDRCS, Save) split across Jamuna (CERF, Agency), Padma (CERF, Agency), Cyclones (excess finance from non-activated), and Total. Key figures: WFP 4,300,000+2,300,000 (Jamuna) / 1,200,000+100,000 (Padma) = 7,900,000 total; FAO 586,541+500,000 / 195,640 = 1,282,181; UNICEF 385,349 / 165,028 = 550,377; UNFPA 925,536+315,000 / 111,347 = 1,351,883; BDRCS 414,760 (Padma agency only) = 414,760; Save 200,000 (Padma agency) = 200,000; Total row: Jamuna CERF 6,197,426 + Agency 3,729,760, Padma CERF 1,672,015 + Agency 100,000; grand total 11,699,201. Second small table "Other anticipatory action with different triggers": START — Jamuna Agency 750,000 (labeled under Padma column in table), Cyclones 600,000.

--- page 7 ---
Narrative text, no figure: CERF section — ERC agreed up to $7.5 million from CERF for Bangladesh AA, disbursed on no-regrets basis once 3 conditions met (RC/HC endorsement + CERF application; ERC pre-approval; activation of readiness or action trigger within max 2 years of pre-approval). Describes disbursement/reimbursement rules and "Learning" section intro (ad-hoc M&E committee convened by OCHA).

Restates readiness/action trigger definitions per basin.
